items.definition: A mineral from food that makes your bones and teeth strong.
items.example: Milk is full of calcium, and calcium keeps my bones strong.

items.definition: A measure of liquid. There are 1000 millilitres in one litre.
items.example: I drink one litre of milk every week.

items.definition: To cut something into thin, flat pieces.
items.example: I slice the banana and put it on top.

items.definition: To cut something into small cubes.
items.example: Please dice the mango for the salad.

items.definition: The liquid water inside a fruit.
items.example: I squeeze some lime juice over the fruit.

items.definition: To make something cold so it tastes fresh.
items.example: We chill the salad in the fridge for one hour.

items.definition: A small amount of food that you eat between two meals.
items.example: I brought a snack to school for break time.

items.definition: To deal with something in a particular way.
The part of food your body cannot digest. It helps your tummy work and keeps you full.
items.example: Wholemeal bread has more fibre than white bread.

items.definition: The building material of your body. It helps you grow and keeps you full for longer.
items.example: Eggs are full of protein, so they are a good snack.

items.definition: The same operation has been applied to both sides.
items.example: The equation stays balanced if you add the same number to both sides.

items.definition: A plant we eat for the part that is not the seed, like a carrot or a cabbage.
items.example: Broccoli and carrot are both vegetables.

items.definition: The part of a plant that grows down into the soil, to hold it up and drink water.
items.example: The root drank the rain deep in the ground.

items.definition: The flat green part of a vegetable that we eat, like cabbage or spinach.
items.example: She washed the leaves in the sink.

items.definition: The firm stem that holds leaves up. Broccoli and bok choy grow on one.
items.example: I eat the stalk of the broccoli too.

items.definition: To cook small pieces of food quickly in a little oil over a hot fire.
items.example: We stir-fry the morning glory for five minutes.

items.definition: The bowl in the bathroom where water comes out. You wash your hands and face in it.
items.example: My hands are under the sink tap.

items.definition: The small handle or knob that turns the water on and off.
items.example: Turn the tap off when you finish washing.

items.definition: The bar or liquid that makes bubbles. Bubbles carry the dirt away with the water.
items.example: There is a new bar of soap by the sink.

items.definition: A soft cloth. You use it to dry your body, your hair and your hands.
items.example: The blue towel is warm and dry.

items.definition: A small brush with bristles. You use it with toothpaste to clean your teeth.
items.example: My toothbrush is green.

items.definition: The soft thing under your head when you sleep in bed.
items.example: My pillow is soft and white.

items.definition: A thick warm cloth that covers you on cold nights.
items.example: I pull the blanket up to my chin.

items.definition: A tall cupboard with a door. You hang your clothes inside it.
items.example: My school uniform hangs in the wardrobe.

items.definition: A flat board on the wall where you keep books and other things.
items.example: There are six books on the shelf.

items.definition: A small clock that rings in the morning to wake you up.
items.example: My alarm clock rings at six.

items.definition: A top with a collar that you wear over your body, on its own or under a jacket.
items.example: My school shirt has a blue collar.

items.definition: Clothes you wear on your legs, one piece for each leg.
items.example: I put on my trousers before my socks.

items.definition: Soft cloth you wear on your feet, inside your shoes.
items.example: These socks are too big for me.

items.definition: Hard things you wear on your feet. One is for the left foot and one for the right.
items.example: I put on my shoes by the door.

items.definition: A thicker top you wear over your shirt when it is cold or wet.
items.example: I wear a jacket when it is cold in the morning.

items.definition: The part of the day from when you wake up until lunchtime.
items.example: In the morning I drink a glass of milk.

items.definition: The middle of the day, around twelve o'clock. It is also called midday.
items.example: We eat lunch at noon.

items.definition: The part of the day after the afternoon. The light gets soft and people come home.
items.example: Good evening, Mum.

items.definition: The woman who looks after you and lives with you.
items.example: My mother works at a shop in the market.

items.definition: A small bowl with a handle. We use it for soup, rice and porridge.
items.example: Can I have a spoon for my soup?

items.definition: A tool with a handle and sharp points. We use it for food in small pieces.
items.example: I eat the fish with a fork.

items.definition: A deep round dish. Soup, cereal and rice porridge go in a bowl.
items.example: There is one bowl of noodles on the table.

items.definition: The cold box in the kitchen. It keeps food fresh for a day or two.
items.example: The eggs are in the fridge.

items.definition: A tall box with doors. Dry food and clean dishes are kept inside it.
items.example: The clean cups are in the cupboard.
